items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Not all bats are the same. Some bats eat fruit, while others eat insects. A few species of bats drink blood from animals. Most bats use echolocation to find food in the dark.

A student says the main topic is 'echolocation.' Is the student correct? Explain using the article.

steps: The student says the main topic is echolocation.
But echolocation is only mentioned in the last sentence.
All the other sentences are about how different bats eat different things.
The whole article is about how bats are different from one another.
So echolocation is a detail, not the main topic.
solution.answer: The student is not correct. Echolocation is only one detail. The main topic is that not all bats are the same, since the article describes different things bats eat.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Many plants protect themselves from being eaten. Roses have thorns on their stems. Cacti have sharp spines all over their bodies. Holly leaves have pointed edges. Some plants even make bitter chemicals that taste bad to animals.

What is the main topic? Which detail do you think is most surprising, and why?

steps: Main topic: many plants protect themselves from being eaten.
Students may choose different details.
A strong answer notes one detail and explains why it is surprising.
For example: It is surprising that plants make bitter chemicals, because plants cannot move or fight, so making bad-tasting chemicals is a clever way to protect themselves without doing anything.
solution.answer: The main topic is that plants protect themselves from being eaten. A surprising detail is that some plants make bitter chemicals, because it shows plants can defend themselves even without moving.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world. It stretches for over 1,400 miles along Australia's coast. Thousands of species of fish and other sea creatures live there. Scientists study it to learn about ocean life.

Write a main topic sentence for this article in your own words. Then list two details.

steps: Students write a sentence that covers what the whole article is about.
Example main topic: The Great Barrier Reef is a huge, important coral reef near Australia.
Detail 1: It stretches over 1,400 miles along Australia's coast.
Detail 2: Thousands of species of fish and sea creatures live there.
solution.answer: Main topic (example): The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef and home to many sea creatures. Two details: it stretches over 1,400 miles, and thousands of species live there.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Some details in an article are important, and some are less important. Read the article and decide.

Whales are the largest animals on Earth. Blue whales can be as long as three school buses. Some people find whales beautiful. Whales breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads.

Which sentence is the least important detail? Explain your thinking.

steps: The main topic is whales as large animals.
Most details are facts: their size, how they breathe.
'Some people find whales beautiful' is an opinion and does not give a factual detail.
This sentence is the least important because it is an opinion, not a fact about whales.
solution.answer: The least important sentence is 'Some people find whales beautiful' because it is an opinion and does not add a fact about whales the way the other details do.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Forests are important for Earth. Trees clean the air by taking in carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen. Forest animals help spread seeds that grow into new trees. Forests also hold soil in place so it does not wash away.

Someone added this sentence to the article: 'I went hiking in a forest once.' Does this sentence belong? Explain.

steps: The main topic is: forests are important for Earth.
All the original sentences give facts about why forests matter.
'I went hiking in a forest once' is a personal story, not a fact about why forests are important.
It does not support the main topic.
So this sentence does not belong in this article.
solution.answer: The sentence does not belong because the main topic is why forests are important, and 'I went hiking in a forest once' is a personal story that does not give a fact about forests.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Animals have different ways of defending themselves. Skunks spray a bad-smelling liquid. Hedgehogs roll into a ball of spines. Octopuses squirt ink to confuse predators.

Write the main topic in your own words. Then add one more detail that could belong in this article.

steps: Main topic: animals have different ways of defending themselves.
Students add a new detail that fits the topic.
Example new detail: Porcupines raise their sharp quills to poke predators that get too close.
solution.answer: Main topic: animals defend themselves in different ways. A new detail that fits: Porcupines raise their sharp quills to protect themselves from predators.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Amazon River is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows through the Amazon rainforest in South America. The river is home to thousands of fish species, including the piranha. It floods every year, spreading rich soil across the land.

What is the main topic? Tell whether each sentence is a main topic sentence or a detail.

steps: Main topic: the Amazon River is one of the longest and most important rivers.
Sentence 1: 'The Amazon River is one of the longest rivers' - main topic sentence.
Sentence 2: 'It flows through the Amazon rainforest' - detail.
Sentence 3: 'home to thousands of fish species' - detail.
Sentence 4: 'It floods every year' - detail.
solution.answer: The main topic is that the Amazon River is one of the world's longest rivers. The first sentence is the main topic; the rest are details about where it is and what it does.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Some animals change their appearance to hide. This is called camouflage. A chameleon can change its skin color to match leaves or bark. The Arctic fox grows white fur in winter to blend with snow. Stick insects look exactly like twigs.

What is the main topic? Why is the word 'camouflage' important to include in a summary?

steps: Main topic: some animals change their appearance to hide, which is called camouflage.
The word 'camouflage' is the key vocabulary word that names this concept.
Any summary of the article would need this word to correctly describe what all the details are about.
Without it, a summary would be missing the name of the main idea.
solution.answer: The main topic is that some animals use camouflage to hide. The word 'camouflage' is important in a summary because it is the name for what all the examples describe.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Vitamins help your body stay healthy. Vitamin C helps your immune system fight sickness. Vitamin D helps your bones grow strong. You can get vitamins by eating fruits, vegetables, and other healthy foods.

A student writes this summary: 'You should eat fruits and vegetables.' Is this a good summary of the main topic? Explain.

steps: The main topic is that vitamins help your body stay healthy.
The student's summary only captures one detail from the last sentence.
It leaves out the main topic and the specific details about Vitamin C and Vitamin D.
A better summary would say: 'Vitamins help your body stay healthy, and you can get them by eating fruits and vegetables.'
solution.answer: It is not a good summary because it only repeats one detail. The main topic is that vitamins help your body stay healthy, which is missing from the student's sentence.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paper is made from wood. Trees are cut down and made into tiny wood chips. The chips are mixed with water and chemicals to make a wet, mushy paste. This paste is pressed flat and dried to make sheets of paper.

Summarize this article in two sentences: one for the main topic and one that combines key details.

steps: Main topic sentence: Paper is made from wood.
Key details: trees are chipped, mixed with water and chemicals to make paste, then pressed and dried.
Combined detail sentence: Trees are cut into chips, mixed with water to make paste, and then pressed and dried into sheets of paper.
solution.answer: Main topic: Paper is made from wood. Details: Trees are cut into chips, mixed with water and chemicals to make a paste, and then pressed flat and dried into sheets of paper.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The savanna is a grassy land in Africa. Tall grasses cover the ground. A few large trees like the baobab grow there. In the wet season, the grass grows tall and green. In the dry season, the grass turns brown.

What is the main topic? Which two details best support it?

steps: Main topic: the savanna is a grassy land in Africa.
Best supporting details: 'Tall grasses cover the ground' and 'In the wet season, grass grows tall and green; in the dry season it turns brown.'
These best support the idea that the savanna is defined by its grasses and seasonal changes.
solution.answer: The main topic is that the savanna is a grassy land in Africa. The two best supporting details are that tall grasses cover the ground and that the grasses change with the seasons.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Some insects are helpful to people. Bees pollinate flowers so fruit can grow. Butterflies also help pollinate plants. Silkworms make silk that people use to make clothing.

Add one more sentence that would be a good detail for this article. Explain why it fits.

steps: Main topic: some insects are helpful to people.
A new detail should give another example of a helpful insect.
Example: Ladybugs eat aphids, which are tiny insects that destroy garden plants.
This fits because it gives another example of an insect helping people.
solution.answer: A new detail: Ladybugs eat aphids that would otherwise destroy garden plants. This fits because it gives another example of a helpful insect, which supports the main topic.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Blood carries oxygen to all parts of your body. Your heart pumps the blood through tubes called veins and arteries. When you exercise, your heart pumps faster to send more oxygen to your muscles.

Write a one-sentence summary of this article that includes the main topic.

steps: Main topic: blood carries oxygen and the heart pumps it.
Key connection: when you exercise, the heart pumps faster.
Summary should capture the main point in one sentence.
solution.answer: Your heart pumps blood through your body to deliver oxygen, and it pumps faster during exercise to meet your muscles' needs.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Cheetahs are the fastest land animals. They can run up to 70 miles per hour. They use their speed to chase and catch prey. However, they can only run that fast for short distances before they get tired.

A student says the main topic is 'cheetahs get tired quickly.' Is the student right? Explain.

steps: The student says the main topic is that cheetahs get tired quickly.
But most of the article is about cheetahs being fast.
Getting tired is only mentioned once in the last sentence as a limitation.
The main topic is that cheetahs are the fastest land animals.
Getting tired quickly is a detail that qualifies their speed.
solution.answer: The student is not right. The main topic is that cheetahs are the fastest land animals. Getting tired quickly is just one detail that explains a limit on their speed.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

There are different types of clouds. Cumulus clouds are puffy and white. Stratus clouds form flat gray sheets. Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy and form high in the sky. The type of cloud can tell you what weather is coming.

What is the main topic? Write a summary that includes the main topic and at least two details.

steps: Main topic: there are different types of clouds.
Detail 1: Cumulus clouds are puffy and white.
Detail 2: Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy and form high in the sky.
Detail 3: The type of cloud can tell you what weather is coming.
solution.answer: There are different types of clouds. Cumulus clouds are puffy and white, cirrus clouds are thin and wispy and form high up, and the type of cloud can tell you what weather is coming.
